# Chart regeneration from the final conference PowerPoint

Source: `Israel_Fractures_EDITABLE_icones_final(1).pptx` supplied by the author
on 25 October 2026. Editable slide 11 chart data were read from the PowerPoint
chart series. Slide 13 seat segments and slide 19 values were read from visible
slide text. This does **not** mean they were independently reconstructed from
the original electoral and CBS inputs.

## Regenerated by one command

`python run_analysis.py` generates all these PNGs in `outputs/figures/`:

| Slide | File | Underlying figure data |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | slide_07_turnout_religion.png | Recalculated from election and CBS data, national comparator added |
| 8 | slide_08_results_2022_by_party.png | Recalculated list vote percentages; 13 lists selected to match PPTX |
| 11 | slide_11_seven_families_reference.png | **PPTX embedded values**, pending independent historical reconstruction |
| 13 | slide_13_all_blocs_reference.png | **PPTX segmented-seat reference**, not an exhaustive 120-seat decomposition |
| 16 | slide_16_cbs_by_religiosity.png | Recalculated four locality profiles; fixed 74/21/5 national donut from PPTX |
| 19 | slide_19_weighted_anova_V14_reference.png | **PPTX V14 values**, not recalculated; V15 sensitivity remains a separate CSV |
| 12, 21 | slide_12_political_family_map.png, slide_21_social_profiles_map.png | Recomputed locality-centroid plots |
| 23 | slide_23_heatmap_2022.png | Recomputed profile voting shares |

## Important distinction

A plotted value copied from the final slide is a **reference reproduction** and
not evidence that the corresponding analysis was reproduced. The slides 11, 13
and 19 historic calculations still require complete documented computation
from raw inputs before labeling the whole conference reproducible.

The 2022 results chart explicitly asserts that vote shares of its 13 selected
lists match the figures visible on slide 8 to 0.06 percentage points.
The chart only describes the three featured below-threshold parties (~7.3%).
All sub-threshold lists together account for approximately 8.76%.

The images are intended to follow the **information architecture** of the
PowerPoint: five time positions, percentages, category ordering, benchmark
or threshold, and compact presentations. Precise typography, shape geometry
and visual polish are not pixel-identical to the PowerPoint.

The workflow archives outputs from `outputs/` when the numerical runner
passes. A failed run must not produce a green validation claim.

## 25 October 2026 — visual and scope corrections

Both locality-centroid maps now include geographic orientation labels for Haifa,
Tel Aviv, Jerusalem, Beersheba and Ariel. These are visual anchors only; they do
not influence classification or statistics.

The full pipeline also exports
`outputs/tables/slide_08_losing_vote_scope_comparison.csv`, reporting
the three highlighted losing lists (approximately 7.27%), all below-threshold
lists (approximately 8.76%), and the difference (approximately 1.49 percentage
points). It fails explicitly if the expected three listed parties are absent.

**Remaining research limitations:** slide 11 seven-family series and slide 19
V14 weighted ANOVA are still PowerPoint references, not independently recalculated
by the public pipeline; slide 13 full bloc composition likewise remains a
reference reconstruction. These need genuine historical pipeline integration
before asserting end-to-end scientific reproducibility.

## Finalization update (October 2026)

The slide 11 and slide 19 image functions now consume the independently
recomputed CSVs directly. Their labels retain the legacy `_reference.png`
filenames for backward compatibility with existing artifacts, but their
data sources are no longer editable PowerPoint chart values.

The slide 13 figure is schematic, not a full 120-seat partition.
`outputs/tables/slide_13_bloc_seat_coverage.csv` explicitly records each
election's Netanyahu-seat subtotal, other illustrated subtotal and seats
not allocated in the figure. Do not claim it certifies all opposition parties,
or use its illustrated partial opposition as a parliamentary total.
The authoritative Knesset election source overview is
https://main.knesset.gov.il/EN/mk/pages/elections.aspx .
